ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L. 561-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier (as amended by Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 and Ordonnance n° 2017-563 of 19 April 2017 implementing EU 5th AML Directive)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign passport or national identity document of UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if country is party) OR Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against French, EU, UN, and OFAC sanctions and PEP lists with ongoing monitoring and annual reviews

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French language mandatory; names must use Latin alphabet; foreign names require transliteration into French
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying unauthorized regulated activities (e.g., banque, assurance without license)
Names confusingly similar to existing entities
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File administrative appeal with the President of the relevant Tribunal de Commerce within two months of rejection notice; subsequent recourse to administrative courts possible

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for administrative purposes provided the address is functional and allows effective management and contact; physical presence required for on-site inspection services
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (5-10%) during pre-incorporation stage; rises to 30-50% during tax or operational audits

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal services for incorporation and statutes drafting
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for standard SARL formation (approx. 1500-2500 EUR)

UBO beneficial ownership registration and compliance setup

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-53 and R.223-1 to R.223-17; general corporate provisions Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10; beneficial ownership declaration under Article L.123-6; Decree No. 2023-205 on business formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce in the jurisdiction of the registered office; electronic intake through the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises managed by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 / Dossier unique d'immatriculation (standardised electronic registration application filed on formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SARL. Every share must be fully subscribed; cash contributions must be paid up to at least 20% at incorporation, with the balance due within five years. Funds are escrowed in a blocked capital deposit account ('attestation de dépôt des fonds') held with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and are released only after the company obtains RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
The Associates, holding the entire share capital of [●] SARL, hereby unanimously resolve:
1. Capital subscription: the [●] shares of €[●] each, representing €[●] capital, are subscribed and paid up in accordance with Article L.223-7 of the Commercial Code.
2. Registered office: the office at [●], France, is formally adopted as the company's statutory registered office.
3. Officers: [Name] is appointed as Gérant, sole manager, with unlimited powers to act on behalf of the company within the corporate purpose.
4. Execution: the Gérant is authorised to sign the incorporation file, deposit capital, publish legal notices, and complete all formalities before the RCS. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the statutory articles of incorporation (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders and legal counsel; private deed sufficient for cash or in-kind contributions excluding real-property assets.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check company name availability in the INPI trademark and corporate-name database; prepare the statuts in French including corporate form, objects, share capital, share subscription, registered office, management powers, and profit allocation. All shares must be fully subscribed. Each associate signs the final deed, either in person or by electronic signature with legal probative value.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address (lease, domiciliation agreement, or title deed)
Contribution appraisal report where in-kind contributions exist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe or notary identifies statutory omissions, correct the statuts through an amending resolution or redraft and obtain fresh signatures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit cash capital in a blocked bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French licensed bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional 'société en formation' capital deposit account in the future company's name after presenting the draft statuts. Transfer the subscribed cash amounts. The bank issues an attestation de dépôt des fonds certifying the amount deposited and the identity of subscribers. The funds remain blocked until the greffe delivers the Kbis registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of each subscribing associate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a query under AML rules, provide updated KYC documents or select another French bank; the attestation is reissued only after the account is fully blocked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the legal announcement in an approved legal-notices journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorised for the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the mandatory insertion text containing the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office address, corporate purpose and first manager. The JAL publishes the notice and issues an attestation de parution. The incorporation filing must reach the RCS within eight days of publication.
required_dossiers: Text of the intended legal notice
Identity and non-conviction declaration of the appointed manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is rejected or contains incomplete statements, publish a corrected version immediately and obtain a fresh attestation before the RCS deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the single incorporation dossier (M0) on the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises, managed by INPI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, select 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée', complete the standardised M0 / dossieunique information, attach scanned supporting documents, pay the prescribed greffe fee, and submit. INPI transmits the file to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and to tax and social authorities.
required_dossiers: Article of legal publication (attestation de parution)
Identity documents of all shareholders and the manager
Declaration of non-conviction of the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS issues a non-opposition or irregularity notice, respond within 15 days through the Guichet Unique portal by amending the statutes or adding missing declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain RCS registration and the official Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After administrative validation, the greffe records the company in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés and issues the Kbis extract, which is the sole conclusive legal identity document of the company. The Kbis permits the bank to release the blocked capital deposit and allows execution of contracts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If delivery of the Kbis is delayed, request a temporary attestation de dépôt from the greffe and use it to open a final bank account or complete lease formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activate final banking, tax and social registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank, DGFiP and URSSAF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Kbis to the bank to transform the provisional account into the company's final account. Verify automatic registration with URSSAF and the tax authorities, confirm SIREN/SIRET numbers, and apply for a TVA intracommunautaire number if the company trades cross-border or invoices French clients.
required_dossiers: Manager's personal tax identification and residence proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF or DGFiP onboarding notices are delayed, use the Kbis to contact the mutualised support of the Guichet Unique and ask for reactivation of the downstream notifications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Implement professional liability insurance and quality management framework
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial insurer/broker; optional COFRAC accreditation pre-assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Subscribe to professional civil liability insurance (RC Professionnelle) covering inspection and testing errors and omissions. Adopt a quality management system aligned with ISO/CEI 17020 or ISO/CEI 17025 if the company seeks accredited inspection reports. Keep the quality manual available for client audits.
required_dossiers: Detailed description of inspection and testing activities
Draft quality manual or operating procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the insurer excludes certain QC mandates, broaden territorial coverage or obtain an additional professional risk policy from another market.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) for environmental and ICPE matters; COFRAC (Comité Français d'Accréditation) for inspection/testing accreditation; DGCCRF for conformity assessment and consumer-safety market surveillance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Accréditation COFRAC selon ISO/CEI 17020:2012 for inspection bodies and/or ISO/CEI 17025:2017 for testing laboratories; where no accredited status is held, the sole statutory operating title is the RCS 'extrait Kbis' obtained under stage 2.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires / DREAL territorialement compétente
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D (normally exempt from full EIA) for a NAF 7120B commercial inspection and QC office; if an on-site laboratory stores dangerous reagents or emits regulated effluents, a preliminary ICPE 'registr' check is required under rubriques 2930/2925, with only the small-package quantities exemption applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to public sewer must meet local arrêté thresholds including pH 6.5-8.5, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L and total suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L; VOC/solvent emissions, if any, must comply with the declared threshold under ICPE rubrique 2931; hazardous waste (solvents, reagents, used oils) must be tracked with BSAD bordereaux and disposed of by a licensed waste contractor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and evacuation certificate issued by the local service de sécurité / commission de sécurité for any premises open to the public; structural load compliance certificate for installed equipment; occupational health clearance from the local occupational health service (médecine du travail) covering the mandatory physical-exams programme and the written 'Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels'.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) with primary portals impots.gouv.fr and portailpro.gouv.fr; SIREN/SIRET issuance by Institut National de la Statistique et des Études Économiques (INSEE) via Répertoire National des Entreprises et des Établissements, interfaced through the INPI/Guichet Unique registration platform; FR VAT number issued separately by the DGFiP Service des Impôts des Entreprises of the competent territorial department.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign investor forms a domestic French SARL through the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), obtaining (1) a SIREN 9-digit identifier and SIRET 14-digit establishment ID via automatic INSEE notification, (2) a Confirmation d'Immatriculation from the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, and (3) an intra-community VAT number. The VAT number is applied for with DGFiP (form CERFA n°14463 for normal VAT regime or via the Guichet Unique when establishing the SARL). The applicant must provide: certified copy of the articles of association (statuts), proof of the registered office address, power of attorney for the non-resident manager, identity documents of shareholders/managers, and declaration of intended activity. VAT registration is delivered in approximately 10-15 working days; the format is FR followed by a 2-digit key and the 9-digit SIREN. For purely intragroup services or subcontracted EU/free-zone functions, a permanent establishment VAT registration could alternatively be required; however, for the standard commercial inspection agency SARL, full ordinary-law TIN/VAT-ID procurement via the SARL is the operative path.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. A SARL is unconditionally subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, Article 206(1) Code Général des Impôts). Optional election: a 'family SARL' owned exclusively by natural-person relatives may elect for partnership-style taxation with 40% abatement under Article 239 bis AA CGI, causing profits to be taxed at the shareholder level (each member taxed on distributable share in the progressive personal income tax schedule); the election is revocable under conditions. Anti-hybrid elections under Article 212 bis CGI (ATAD transposition) apply to hybrid financial instruments and hybrid entities: French entities must classify each foreign partnership or transparent entity for French tax purposes according to its foreign legal form, and an election to re-characterize a disregarded foreign entity as transparent or opaque may be made where the foreign treaty classification so provides. Additionally, a SARL may elect between the simplified real VAT regime (régime réel simplifié) and the normal real VAT regime (régime réel normal) on form CA 707, but such elections do not alter entity-level income tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (Value Added Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory nationwide e-invoicing and e-reporting reform in phases: B2B domestic e-invoicing and B2C e-reporting obligations begin 1 September 2026 for large enterprises (grandes entreprises) and 1 September 2027 for SMEs/general taxpayers. All VAT-registered persons established in France must transmit structured e-invoices via an accredited Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the State platform (Portail Public de Facturation, 'Chorus Pro'). Mandatory formats are Factur-X (hybrid), UBL, or CII. There is no digital fiscal stamp or real-time transaction clearance server; instead, invoice lifecycle statuses (issued, received, paid) and invoice registration data are transmitted to DGFiP in near-real-time, under the FNN (Facturation dans le Nuage National) architecture. Parallel obligations require French accounting book files to be produced in the FEC (Fichier des Écritures Comptables) standard and retained for at least 6 years (10 years for real estate activities, situational).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 262 CGI, exports of tangible goods dispatched or transported to a destination outside the European Union are exempt from French VAT (zero-rated) when the direct proof of physical exit from EU customs territory is held. Intra-Community supplies of goods are exempt pursuant to Article 262 ter CGI if the transferee supplies a valid French or other-Union VAT number and movement justifying evidence is compiled. For a factory-inspection/QC agency, the following qualifying scenarios apply: (i) testing, inspection and audit services physically supplied on goods that are then exported and provided to a non-French principal are zero-rated if the services directly relate to the goods and are covered by the Article 262 zero-rating shadow; (ii) B2B services rendered to a customer established outside the EU fall outside the territorial scope of French VAT under Article 259 A CGI (place of supply is the customer's place of business), without application of the 20% rate and without requiring a separate invoice; (iii) services to EU B2B customers are taxable in the customer's Member State where the customer is established and do not trigger French VAT output. Entry cannot be claimed by mere declaration; the taxpayer must retain contemporaneous, consistent trade documents.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Document Unique d'Accompagnement / Document Administratif Unique generated through the DELTA-H/ Télé-Douane system, with registered MRN)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR International Consignment Note evidencing physical transportation
Commercial invoices, the fixed-price export contract and signed inspection/QC reports or certificates of conformity
Proof of delivery and customs exit certificate (certificat d'origine, transit documents or customs stamp)
Inward remittance certificate (relevé de remise bancaire) and corresponding SWIFT/Wise settlement records matching invoice currency and debtor name
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax authority rigorously audits export zero-rating claims under Articles 262 and 262 ter CGI and can claw back VAT, impose intérêt de retard of 0.20% per month (2.4% annualized), a 5% late-payment penalty, and an additional 40% bad-faith penalty (Article 1729 CGI) or 80% for organised abuse or simulated acts (Article 1729-0 CGI). Material misstatements trigger fines of €500 per irregular document under Article 1737 CGI and up to €750 per documentary falsehood under the general penal provisions. Tax fraud prosecution under Article 1741 CGI carries imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines up to €500,000 (extended to 7 years and €2,000,000 when committed by an organized gang). The use of artificial arrangements solely to obtain export exemption is recharacterized under Article L64 LPF (abus de droit) with a 80% penalty plus interest. Retention of the export documentation bundle is compulsory for at least 6 years under Article L102 B Livre des Procédures Fiscales, and refunds may be audited retrospectively within the normal three-year limitation period, extended to six years where tax fraud is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (central bank and balance-of-payments statistical authority); ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) as banking licensing and supervisory authority; Direction Générale du Trésor within the Ministry of Economy and Finance exercises capital-movement policy. The Banque de France operates the external financial statistics (balance des paiements) declaration regime and is the authority to which corporate cross-border financial flows are reported.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone member with unrestricted euro convertibility. Under Article 63 TFEU and the EU Capital Movements Directive (88/361/EEC), France fully liberalises both current-account and capital-account transactions for non-residents; no exchange-control approvals apply to equity injections, loans, dividends, royalties, or service fees denominated in EUR or foreign currency. Practical residual hurdles: (i) commercial banks require a documented economic purpose and complete KYC for each flow; (ii) dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders attract French withholding tax at 30% (or a reduced treaty rate) under Code Général des Impôts Article 119 bis; (iii) all international transfers must be effected through banking intermediation under the Code Monétaire et Financier; (iv) foreign-currency accounts may be held, but the underlying business justification must be evidenced. Profit remittance is therefore legally unconstrained, subject only to tax documentation and anti-money-laundering controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no mandatory export-proceeds surrender rule and no statutory conversion ratio or repatriation deadline. Export invoices may be settled in EUR or any freely convertible currency, and proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts opened with French credit institutions. Residual obligations: (i) all export receipts and trade payments must flow through a licensed credit institution (financial intermediation rule); (ii) invoices and underlying contracts must evidence economic reality when requested by the bank; (iii) a balance-of-payments declaration must be filed with the Banque de France for any year in which aggregate cross-border financial flows equal or exceed EUR 750,000, with detailed reporting per counterparty; and (iv) individual transfers of EUR 10,000 or more remain subject to automated AML screening and documentary retention.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte Bloqué) for statutory share-capital deposit, convertible to Operational Treasury Account in EUR/USD/GBP after registration
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Multi-Currency Account (compte courant, compte en devises)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Group (LCL S.A. — LCL Entreprises)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Professional Operational Account with dedicated blocked subscription account for SARL capital formation

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE Group (Banque Populaire / Caisse d'Épargne, BPCE S.A.)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency operational account; statutory capital escrow available through branch dépôt de fonds

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for routine low-value treasury operations through French-registered EMIs (Qonto, Shine, PENEXO) and EU-passported EMIs (Wise Europe S.A. under Belgian EMI licence) for collections, supplier payouts, and expense cards; LOW for statutory SARL formation because the capital-blocking requirement for apport en numéraire mandates a licensed credit institution or a notary, not an electronic money institution. Legal constraints: EMIs under PSD2 may issue e-money but may not take deposits, issue documentary letters of credit, execute FX forwards or options, or serve as the main correspondent trade-clearing channel; balance-of-payments reporting remains the French bank's intermediary duty. Recommended architecture: French tier-1 bank as house bank and statutory escrow provider; an EMI used only as a supplementary low-value disbursement rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one gérant (director) and each natural-person UBO holding more than 25% is the de facto rule at tier-1 French banks for first-time non-resident corporate account opening; ACPR remote-onboarding guidelines permit video identification only with qualified eIDAS signatures or certified facial-verification technology, which is rarely accepted for third-country nationals. EU/EEA passport holders may access video onboarding at selected banks, including BNP Paribas and Qonto. The account-opening interview covers corporate purpose, factory-inspection business model, principal and subcontractor concentration, source of shareholder funds, expected wire volumes, and FX/hedging perimeter. The documentary bundle must include passports, proof of address, registered-office lease, Kbis excerpt, Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) receipt, shareholders' register, and an executed treasury authority matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity — missing or inconsistent beneficial-ownership declaration between the share register and the RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) extract filed at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised or legalised UBO schedule naming each natural-person shareholder of 25% or more; RBE filing receipt; passports and national ID copies of all UBOs; corporate organisation chart of the non-resident parent; certificate of good standing; signed treasury mandate listing authorised executing directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk inflow classification — inbound capital injection appears sourced from a corporate treasury rather than the personal shareholder account of a named UBO, or from a third-party lender without equity documentation, suggesting pass-through or concealment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extraordinary General Meeting minutes with capital-increase resolution; bank certificate of deposit of funds (attestation de dépôt des fonds); source-of-funds bank statements in the shareholder's own name; share subscription bulletin; sworn statement that no loan or encumbrance backs the contribution; notarised declaration of accuracy under French law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No-real-activity pattern — inspection-agency flows show high wire volume disproportionate to payroll, triggering ACPR 'marchand de liquidités' (money-service) typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISO/IEC 17020 accreditation certificate; master service agreements with principals; geotagged and dated factory inspection reports; test-results chain-of-custody logs; professional-indemnity insurance; staffing contracts and payroll proof; multi-year P&L versus projected cash-flow model; picture of sample custody and calibration certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FX/hedging misuse — treasury requests for forwards, options, or non-deliverable structures without a verifiable open exposure, including attempted NDF on the fully convertible EUR/USD cross, triggering market-abuse and disguise-prevention screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury hedging policy approved by the gérant; board resolution limiting hedges to a maximum of 85% of firm billed exposure; USD/GBP receivable inventory with ageing; prior-month conversion evidence in trial balance; each hedge position reconcilable to an invoiced inspection order and master service agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP adjacency — counterparty or end-factory in the non-EEA inspection supply chain (China, Vietnam, India, Bangladesh) generates counterparty-sanction flags and refusal of remittance instructions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening evidence against EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, and UN sanctions; end-user confirmation letter; transaction-country rationale memo; full KYC of subagent or foreign factory including trade-registry certificate, tax ID, passport, and beneficial ownership data; contractual prohibition on sanctioned goods and services.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) open a statutory capital blocked account (compte bloqué) at a French credit institution or deposit funds with a notary before SARL registration; (2) remit via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for an EU-resident parent) from the shareholder's own account, quoting ISO 20022 purpose code IVCA (Investment Capital) and the free-text reference 'APPORT EN CAPITAL — FR_SARL — SIREN PENDING'; (3) use TARGET2 settlement through the French bank's correspondent for non-EEA wires, with the beneficiary IBAN of the blocked account and the bank's French BIC; (4) no Banque de France FX approval applies, but enhanced AML verification is triggered when the remitter name does not match the shareholder register or when the amount equals or exceeds EUR 10,000; (5) the French bank issues the certificat de dépôt des fonds enabling the gérant to apply for company registration; (6) funds are released to the operational treasury account only upon production of the Kbis and filed Articles of Association; (7) the SARL records the contribution in the shareholders' register and, where annual aggregate cross-border flows reach EUR 750,000, files the Banque de France direct-investment declaration for 'investissement direct — apport en capital en numéraire'.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rail strategy for factory inspection, QC testing, and audit payables: (a) EU/EEA subcontractors and calibration laboratories are settled through SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR with purpose code COMC/TRAD and a VAT reverse-charge invoice reference; (b) non-EEA vendors are settled through SWIFT MT103 in the invoice currency (USD, GBP, CNY, EUR) via the house bank's correspondent network; (c) high-value export-critical deliverables are secured through irrevocable sight or usance Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600, with payment against presentation of inspection certificates, test reports, and cargo documents; (d) low-value operational payments below EUR 10,000 may use the Wise Europe EMI rail, but Wise cannot provide documentary LC or FX forward capacity; (e) every disbursement is matched to an approved purchase order, inspection deliverable, and signed acceptance report; (f) restricted-country counterparties require additional OFAC/EU sanction screening and end-use statements; (g) foreign-currency payouts are settled either from forward contracts or from natural hedging where the company holds matching USD or GBP inspection receivables.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward (change à terme) on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CNY for maturities up to 12 months, subject to an approved treasury limit and board resolution.
FX swap (swap de change) for short-term intra-month liquidity alignment between inspection-fee receivables and vendor payouts.
Cross-currency swap (swap de devises) for matched-term hedging of long USD-denominated master service agreements and structural balance-sheet exposure.
Plain-vanilla FX option purchases (long call and long put) with premium settled upfront, permitted on a hedge-only basis with no naked option writing.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) limited to currencies without full convertibility (onshore CNY variants, INR, BRL, VND) where a documented underlying inspection contract exists in that currency and settlement is effected through EUR offset with full audit trail.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (plus a 3.3% social surcharge when the income tax after the normal rate exceeds EUR 763,000, producing a top effective rate of 25.825%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for eligible SMEs; research tax credit (CIR) at 30% and innovation tax credit (CII) at 20%; other deductions for export, headquarters, and innovation activities.
